finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /settings/email runs the email-change operation with uid=None. login_optional never aborts, so the account-mutating handler is reachable anonymously. Severity HIGH: the set_email sink is a stub, so account impact is not demonstrable from this file (CRITICAL downgraded per triage Check 13 Q5).
finding.source: Anonymous HTTP POST to /settings/email (no session cookie)

trace.note: g.uid = session.get('uid') yields None for anonymous clients
Wrapped handler called with no abort (contrast login_required lines 11-12)
set_email(None, 'new@example.org') executes; input ignored, constant written
Sink body is 'pass'; real effect unknown from this file

finding.guards_checked: login_optional does not abort (routes.py:19-25); no CSRF token; no body validation; no re-authentication; no rate limit; no gateway config in repo

verdict.guard_found: none. login_optional (routes.py:19-25) only assigns g.uid = session.get("uid") and never aborts, unlike login_required (routes.py:11-12). change_email (routes.py:34-38) calls set_email(g.uid, ...) with no check on g.uid, no CSRF or body validation, and no re-authentication. Only an external gateway could block this, and the repo contains no such config.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: login_optional at routes.py:19-25 never aborts, so the anonymous POST to /settings/email reaches set_email(None, ...) at routes.py:37 with no guard. The stub sink at routes.py:48-49 limits how much account impact this file can demonstrate, but it does not block reachability, so the finding stands at the reported HIGH severity.

finding.claim: Any authenticated session can set the account password to the hardcoded literal 'hunter2' with no current-password or re-auth check, giving persistent account takeover. Also a hardcoded credential literal applied to real accounts. Severity HIGH.
finding.source: Authenticated session cookie for account U; POST /settings/password (request body ignored)

trace.note: 'uid' in session check; abort(401) if absent
Hardcoded literal 'hunter2' passed as new password for g.uid
Sink body is 'pass'; real effect assumed to persist a password

finding.guards_checked: login_required session check present (necessary, not sufficient); no current-password or re-auth check; no input read so no input validation; no CSRF token; no rate limit; literal is not a placeholder

verdict.guard_found: login_required (routes.py:8-16, checks session 'uid' at line 11 and aborts 401) is the only control. It is authentication, not re-authentication: there is no current-password or re-auth check, no CSRF token, and no rate limit anywhere in routes.py. The /settings/password handler (routes.py:41-45) reads no request body and passes the literal "hunter2" to set_password unconditionally.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: the route is registered at routes.py:41, login_required at routes.py:42 only checks that a session uid exists (routes.py:11-13), and routes.py:44 passes the fixed literal "hunter2" to set_password, so any holder of an authenticated session can set that account's password to a known value without knowing the current one. The attacker is an authenticated user for the target account (for example, someone holding a hijacked session), which is a real escalation from temporary session access to a persistent credential. The effect itself is a stub (routes.py:52-53 is `pass`), so the persisted takeover is inferred, not shown in this repo.

finding.claim: State-changing POST endpoints /settings/email and /settings/password authenticate only by cookie-based Flask session with no CSRF token and no SameSite configuration in this file. Retained at MEDIUM because it weaponises AUTH-2; exploitability depends on browser SameSite defaults, which usually block cross-site POSTs.
